verdict: J.B. Hunt's revenue jumped 20% to $3.68B — lifted by fuel surcharges and surging brokerage volumes — but net earnings barely grew, to $172M, as purchased transportation, driver and insurance costs ate the gains.

segments.name: Intermodal (JBI)
segments.note: Containers moving by rail and truck — loads rose 8%, with the Eastern network up 18% as freight converts from road to rail. Segment operating income rose 18% to $148M.

segments.name: Dedicated Contract Services (DCS)
segments.note: Trucks and drivers run exclusively for one customer — revenue up 11%, but profit fell 22% on driver pay, medical and insurance costs.

segments.name: Integrated Capacity Solutions (ICS)
segments.note: The freight brokerage — matching shippers with third-party trucks. Volume rose 22% and the segment swung to a $9.6M profit.

segments.name: Truckload (JBT)
segments.note: One-way full-truckload shipping — revenue per load up 29%.

segments.name: Final Mile Services (FMS)
segments.note: Delivering big items like furniture and appliances to homes — shrinking on purpose as J.B. Hunt exits low-quality business.

opex.name: Salaries, wages & benefits
opex.note: Pay for drivers and staff — the biggest in-house cost, up 7%.

opex.name: Fuel & fuel taxes
opex.note: Diesel for the fleet — up sharply with fuel prices and surcharges.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of trucks and containers over their lives.

opex.name: Operating supplies & expenses
opex.note: Day-to-day supplies and running expenses across the network.

opex.name: Insurance & claims
opex.note: Insurance premiums and accident claims — up 23% year over year.

opex.name: General, administrative & other
opex.note: Back office, asset dispositions, operating taxes, licenses and communications.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $16M on about $1.12B of debt, down from $1.60B a year ago.

takeaways.title: The brokerage is booming
takeaways.text: ICS revenue surged 57% on 22% more volume and 29% higher revenue per load, swinging the segment from a small loss to a $9.6M profit.

takeaways.title: Fuel inflates the growth rate
takeaways.text: Fuel surcharge revenue nearly doubled to $671M as fuel prices rose. Excluding surcharges, revenue grew 13% — still strong, but not 20%.

takeaways.title: Dedicated profit got squeezed
takeaways.text: DCS grew revenue 11% yet its operating income fell 22% to $82M, hit by driver pay, group medical claims and insurance costs.

footerNote: J.B. Hunt's statement groups all running costs as operating expenses; this page treats rents and purchased transportation — paying railroads and outside carriers — as the direct cost of revenue. Segment revenues are the company's rounded headline figures; Intermodal absorbs an $8M rounding difference so the segments add to total revenue.
